purpose: ROADMAP 1.3 asks for a checker different in KIND, not just in authorship,
because the two kernels this repository runs implement the same algorithm
-- and, as ROADMAP 1.3a records, one is derived from the other's C++
original. This is the evaluation of the candidate that is different in
kind: con-leche, whose acceptance of a declaration set is PROVED in Lean
to imply that the set has a model in set theory.

checker.name: con-leche
authorship_note: Upstream states that the checker and its consistency proof were written
by Claude (Fable and Opus) under supervision by Joachim Breitner at the
Lean FRO. Recorded because this repository is itself about AI-assisted
proof work, and because it cuts the way this repository argues about its
own artefacts: what makes the checker worth trusting is a machine-checked
theorem, not who or what typed it.
checker.built: the FULL build, 660 Lake jobs, including the proof lane (ConLeche.MainTheorem). A verified kernel whose verification one has not built is not evidence of anything.

the_theorem.how_checked: #print axioms on both, against the build produced here
the_theorem.what_it_says: model_exists: if checkDecls accepts a declaration array in verified mode, the resulting environment has a model in a set theory V. no_False_declaration: a file declaring a theorem of type False is never accepted.
the_hypothesis_not_discharged_here: Both theorems are parameterised over `(V : Type w) [SetTheory V]` -- an
interface for ZF without infinity and choice, plus an omega-chain of
Grothendieck universes in Tarski form. The theorems are CONDITIONAL on
Upstream discharges that from Mathlib's ZFSet under Carneiro's
package. THAT PACKAGE WAS NOT BUILT HERE (it needs Mathlib at con-leche's
toolchain). So what was verified on this machine is the conditional
statement, not the instantiation of its hypothesis.

runs.input: AmpasRef.Guards (the trusted reference environment and its guards)
runs.message: not implemented yet: use of the sorryAx axiom in value of Ampas.Claims.pl_bogus_independent
runs.reading: Correct, and it is about AMPAS's design rather than about con-leche: the reference module states each frozen claim as `theorem ... := sorry`, so the environment contains sorryAx in a value by construction. The reference environment therefore CANNOT be checked by con-leche as such; what can be checked is a submission's own closure.

runs.input: corpus/Genuine.lean (a genuine submission, certified by AMPAS)
runs.reading: The result that matters for ROADMAP 1.3: a genuine submission's entire closure -- the proof plus all of Init/Lean/Std it depends on -- is accepted by a checker whose acceptance is proved to imply a set-theoretic model. Cheaper than expected: 43 seconds and 0.39 GiB on two cores.

runs.input: corpus/attacks/A04_native_lie.lean (native_decide; BOTH Lean kernels accept it)
reading: Both Lean kernels accept this submission (kernel_replay: true,
kernel_replay_independent: true, in evidence/corpus_results_threechecks.json).
con-leche does not. So a checker different in kind does refuse
something the Lean kernels take.
BUT READ THE REASON BEFORE CREDITING IT. The refusal is con-leche's
AXIOM RESTRICTION -- it accepts only the three standard axioms -- which
is the same layer AMPAS's own axiom policy already occupies, and which
already flags this submission as NATIVE_EVALUATION. The model-theoretic
proof did no work here. Calling this 'the verified kernel caught an
attack the Lean kernels accepted' would be exactly the overclaim
ROADMAP 1.3a corrects about lean4lean.
Note also that 'not implemented yet' is a DECLINE, not a rejection on
the merits. A decline is not evidence that a proof is wrong.

runs.input: corpus/attacks/A06_wrong_statement.lean (a real proof of `∀ a, a + a = a + a` filed as `add_comm_nat`)
reading: THE HEADLINE RESULT, and it is a negative one. A checker whose
acceptance is PROVED to imply a set-theoretic model accepts a genuine
proof of the wrong statement, because the proof is genuine and the
statement is a theorem -- just not the claim it is filed under.
So the fidelity gap is not a weakness of unverified kernels that a
verified one closes. It is outside what ANY kernel decides, however
strong its soundness proof. In AMPAS only the statement comparator and
a human reading stand between this submission and a certificate, and
adding con-leche would not change that by one step. ASSUMPTIONS A1.

note: The Lean Kernel Arena benchmarks ~28 Lean proof checkers against shared
suites: soundness (proofs that must be rejected), completeness (proofs
that must be accepted), 19 bug-regression tests, corner cases and
performance. It is third-party and adversarial, which is what ROADMAP 6
asks for and what nothing in this repository can supply about itself.
As read on 2026-10-14 it reported con-leche with 0 wrongly accepted and 0
wrongly rejected, 3 soundness and 6 completeness declines, and mathlib in
~24.7 min / 7.1 GB; and lean4lean with 0 wrongly accepted, 0 wrongly
rejected, and mathlib in ~38.8 min / 11.6 GB. Those numbers are the
arena's, not this repository's, and a round was in progress when read.

verdict.what_it_adds: A third acceptance whose meaning is not 'another implementation agrees' but 'the accepted declaration set has a model in set theory'. Against the Tao finding -- that two implementations can share a failure -- and against ROADMAP 1.3a -- that this repository's second kernel is derived from the first -- that is a genuinely different kind of evidence.
what_it_does_not_add: Anything about formalization fidelity (the A06 run).
Anything the axiom policy does not already catch on the attack corpus
An unconditional soundness guarantee: the theorem is conditional on a
set theory interface whose instantiation was not built here.
A check of AMPAS's reference environment, which contains `sorry` by
integration_decision: Recorded as an OPTIONAL tier, scripts/check-with-conleche.sh, and not
wired into verify.sh's default path. The reasons are cost, not doubt: it
needs a second 3 GB toolchain (Lean 4.35.0-rc3 against this suite's
4.33.0), a 660-job build of the checker and its proofs, a build of
lean4export at v4.33.0 to read this suite's oleans, and a ~333 MB NDJSON
export per submission. Making that a default would make a clean checkout
What IS wired in: nothing silently. A certificate does not claim a
con-leche acceptance unless one was run and recorded.
